post.title: World Cup 2026 Semifinals: One Safe Bet, One Coin Flip

tweets.text:
Semifinals: One Safe Bet, One Coin Flip

Both Semifinal ties are set, with very different value gaps. France-Spain sits at 1.25x — favorites have won 24 of 33 comparable matches since 2006. England-Argentina's 1.69x is close to a coin flip.

Thread 🧵

France vs Spain: A Deeper Squad, But Not Everywhere

France's squad (€1,523m) beats Spain's (€1,223m) by €300m, mostly in attack (1.76x). But Spain's midfield actually leads, and Lamine Yamal (€200m) outprices Mbappé as the priciest player here.

Mbappé's Output Dwarfs Spain's Entire Response

Kylian Mbappé (€180m) has 11 combined goal contributions this tournament — more than Spain's entire top 10 combined. Lamine Yamal, the board's priciest player at €200m, has managed just 1.

At 1.25x, Favorites Win — But Rarely Comfortably

The closest historical matches to this gap were tight almost without exception — 4 of 5 finished 1-0. Portugal supplies two: beaten by Spain this tournament, and by France in the 2006 Semifinal.

At 1.25x, France Wrote Half the Underdog Blueprint

Two of the five closest upsets at this gap belong to France itself — beating Brazil 1-0 in 2006 and England 2-1 in 2022, both as the cheaper side.

Zoom Out: 33 Matches, Nine Went the Other Way

Every knockout match within 0.3x of this 1.25x gap — 33 since 2006 — and favorites won 24 of them. The nine upsets, France's pair included, are the exception, not the rule.

England vs Argentina: Even at Midfield, a Gulf at the Back

England's squad (€1,358m) beats Argentina's (€808m) by 68% — but midfield is nearly level. Defence is the opposite story: England's back line costs 2.5x Argentina's, the widest gap of the five.

Kane Matches Bellingham at Half the Price

Jude Bellingham (€130m) leads with 7 combined goal contributions, but Harry Kane matches that exact tally at just €60m. Messi remains the matchup's most productive player outright — valued at just €15m.

At 1.69x, Argentina's Already Been Here — and Lost

Argentina stood on nearly this exact gap before: the €900m underdog against France's €1,616m in the 2018 Round of 16. They lost 4-3, the highest-scoring match in this entire comparison set.

At 1.69x, England's Already Lost a Semifinal Here

England has been upset from nearly this gap twice — on penalties vs Portugal in 2006, and 2-1 outright against Croatia in the 2018 Semifinal, the same round England plays tonight.

Zoom Out: Nearly a Coin Flip

Every knockout match within 0.3x of this 1.69x gap — 24 in total — and the split holds: 13 favorites, 11 upsets. The less predictable of the two Semifinal gaps, by a wide margin.
